title: 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 Triangles
short: Their sides are in fixed ratios: 1 : 1 : √2 and 1 : √3 : 2.
trouble: Students put √3 on the hypotenuse or match it to the wrong leg.

blocks.html: Two right triangles show up so often that their side ratios are worth knowing by heart. Both come straight from the Pythagorean theorem of Proving the Pythagorean Theorem with Similarity, and their answers use the simplified square roots from Simplifying Square Roots.

45-45-90: cut a square with side $s$ along a diagonal. Each half is an isosceles right triangle with legs $s$, so its hypotenuse is $\sqrt{s^2 + s^2} = \sqrt{2s^2} = s\sqrt{2}$.
30-60-90: cut an equilateral triangle with side $2s$ by its altitude. Each half has angles $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, hypotenuse $2s$, and shorter leg $s$ (half of the base). The longer leg is $\sqrt{(2s)^2 - s^2} = \sqrt{3s^2} = s\sqrt{3}$.

blocks.cap: Half a square (left) and half an equilateral triangle (right).

opts.label: Half of a square makes a 45-45-90 triangle; half of an equilateral triangle makes a 30-60-90 triangle

blocks.html: 45-45-90: sides $s : s : s\sqrt{2}$. 30-60-90: sides $s : s\sqrt{3} : 2s$, with $s$ opposite $30^\circ$, $s\sqrt{3}$ opposite $60^\circ$ and $2s$ (the hypotenuse) opposite $90^\circ$.

blocks.title: A 45-45-90 triangle
blocks.q: (a) The legs are $7$. Find the hypotenuse. (b) The hypotenuse is $10$. Find a leg.

blocks.title: From the hypotenuse of a 30-60-90 triangle
blocks.q: The hypotenuse is $14$. Find both legs.

blocks.title: From the longer leg
blocks.q: The longer leg of a 30-60-90 triangle is $9$. Find the shorter leg and the hypotenuse.

blocks.html: Putting $\sqrt{3}$ on the hypotenuse, or on the leg next to the $60^\circ$ angle. Match sizes: the longest side ($2s$) faces the biggest angle ($90^\circ$), and the shortest side ($s$) faces the smallest angle ($30^\circ$). Since $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ is between 1 and 2, $s\sqrt{3}$ is the middle side, across from $60^\circ$.
